Pseudonymize subject identifiers consistently across datasets

Source: R/anon_subject.R
anon_subject_ids.Rd

Replaces each subject's key (for example USUBJID) with a random pseudonym that is the same in every dataset, so the datasets can still be joined. Related identifier columns listed in also (for example SUBJID) are replaced with the pseudonym's number so they stay aligned with the key, and columns listed in key_cols that hold other subjects' keys (for example RSUBJID) are mapped through the same pseudonyms.

Usage

anon_subject_ids(
  data,
  key = "USUBJID",
  also = "SUBJID",
  key_cols = "RSUBJID",
  prefix = "SUBJ-",
  keep_secrets = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  other_attributes = c("rewrite", "drop")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, a named list of data frames linked by key, or the result of an earlier step such as anon_subject_dates(). In datasets without the key column the values are left unchanged; keys in their attributes and names are rewritten (see Details).

key

Name of the subject identifier column.

also

Names of related identifier columns that hold one value per subject (default "SUBJID"). They are replaced with the pseudonym's number. Columns not present in a dataset are skipped.

key_cols

Names of columns that hold subject keys, possibly of other subjects (default "RSUBJID", as in SDTM RELSUB). Each value is replaced with that subject's pseudonym; values that are not a known key are removed with a warning.

prefix

Prefix for character pseudonyms, followed by a zero-padded number (e.g. "SUBJ-042"). Numeric keys get the number itself.

keep_secrets

Logical. If TRUE, keep the mapping from keys to pseudonyms; read it with anon_secrets(). Default FALSE: the mapping is not kept anywhere.

seed

Optional seed for the random assignment, for reproducible tests. Anyone with the seed and the original data can rebuild the mapping, so do not set it for data you share. The global random number state is restored afterwards.

other_attributes

What to do with attributes beyond the core ones (variable and dataset labels, comments, haven value labels and user-defined missing values, and names, which are always rewritten): custom text attributes, list- and data frame-valued attributes, Date or factor values held in attributes, and attributes of attributes. "rewrite" (default) rewrites what it can find in them, at any depth, as a best effort. "drop" removes them, and is the strict choice: nothing can hide in an attribute that is gone. Structural attributes are never dropped, and are structural only on the classes that use them: class, names, row.names, dim and dimnames on anything; levels and contrasts on factors; tzone on date-times; units on difftime and units objects; tsp on time series; type and states on survival::Surv objects; ptype on vctrs objects (its text is still rewritten); groups on grouped and rowwise tibbles; sorted, index and .internal.selfref on data.tables; SAS, SPSS and Stata formats, and a numeric display_width, on vectors. Elsewhere an attribute with one of these names is text (for example free-text units on a number). The log counts the attributes dropped in each dataset.

Value

An object of class "anon_deid_step": a list with data (the transformed data, in the same form as the input), log (a tibble with step, dataset, variable, n_changed, n_removed and detail; the first row of each step records its settings; earlier steps are included when data was a step result), settings (a named list with each step's arguments, without the seed value) and secrets (NULL unless keep_secrets = TRUE here or in an earlier step). Saving the object (for example with saveRDS()) also saves its secrets.

Details

Pseudonyms are numbered in random order, and rows of each dataset are then sorted by the new key (keeping the order of rows within each subject), so neither the pseudonyms nor the row order reveal the order of the original keys. Column types and attributes such as variable labels are kept (original keys in their text are rewritten, see below). Character keys get character pseudonyms, numeric keys get numbers, factors stay factors. Value labels (haven labels), which describe the original values, are dropped from replaced columns. Missing and blank keys are left as they are. Values of also columns in rows without a key cannot be mapped and are removed (set to missing), with a warning. key, also and key_cols must not overlap.

Original keys in text that describes the data are replaced with the subject's pseudonym, in every dataset (with or without key), when they appear as a whole value or a whole word: in the attributes of columns, data frames and the list of datasets (such as label, comment or a custom note), at any depth (text in list or factor attributes, the values of data frames held in attributes, names of attribute vectors, attributes of attributes, attribute names); in the names of vector columns and the dimnames of matrix columns; in haven value labels of columns that are not replaced (the label names, and the label values of character columns) and in character user-defined missing values (na_values, na_range) of those columns; and in column names, character row names and dataset names. Structural attributes (see other_attributes) are left alone, except that text in a vctrs ptype, and the names of a factor's contrasts matrix, are rewritten; a factor whose values are replaced or shifted drops a contrasts matrix (named by its old levels, it no longer fits the new ones), and keeps a contrasts function's name such as "contr.sum". So are environments, functions and S4 objects held in attributes (they can refer to themselves, are shared with whoever else holds them, or must keep valid slots; S4 objects are named in a warning). The grouping of a grouped or rowwise tibble (groups) and the key and indices of a data.table (sorted, index) are renamed with the columns. A grouped tibble held in an attribute has its grouping values rewritten with its values. With other_attributes = "drop", attributes beyond the core ones are dropped instead of rewritten. A label value or missing-value code is rewritten only when no value of the column equals it or its rewrite (or, for na_range, falls in either range), so the mapping from values to labels and which values are missing don't change; a code kept this way is named in a warning, as is a missing-value range whose rewritten ends would be in descending order. Value labels whose codes the rewrite made equal are merged into one entry, their original labels joined with " / " and then rewritten (haven requires distinct codes; label text may repeat), and equal missing-value codes are deduplicated; a warning names each. Ranges are compared as R compares text in the session's collation, as haven does. A rewritten name that clashes with another gets a numeric suffix ("_1"), and settings and the log name the suffixed column; a column name in the settings that was renamed differently in different datasets is rewritten as text instead. Column and dataset names marked as "bytes" are handled like other names and stay marked as "bytes" unless rewritten. A dataset with nothing to rewrite is returned as the same object, so := on a data.table changes the input too; once a later step changes it, its .internal.selfref is stale (call data.table::setDT()). Keys made only of digits, and numeric keys, are not rewritten, for the same reason they are not searched for below. The log has one row per dataset with such rewrites (and one for the list of datasets), with counts by kind; this and earlier steps' logs and settings are renamed and rewritten to match. Values in the data are not rewritten, including the elements of list columns and packed data frame columns, with everything inside them: a packed column's own attributes (even its label) and names are left as they are, and handling nested data is planned.

A warning lists any other character or factor column (values or factor levels), list column (all the text its elements hold: values, factor levels, names and attributes, at any depth), or column of a packed data frame column (named as dataset.column[subcolumn], and deeper as dataset.column[sub][subsub], with the text in its attributes; the packed column itself is named for its column names and attributes), in any dataset, that still contains original key values as whole values or as whole words inside text (checked for character keys that are not made only of digits, since numbers match many unrelated codes), and any dataset without key that has a column named like key, also or key_cols in any case. In datasets with key, a column named like one of them in another case (such as usubjid beside USUBJID) is not replaced and is named in a warning. Only text or factor columns can be given in key_cols; the others must be redacted or removed. Locations printed in warnings have keys rewritten, as names inside packed columns can hold them. Columns of S4 objects are not searched or changed, and are named in a warning as data that can't be checked. Original values of also columns (such as SUBJID) elsewhere are not checked, because short numbers match many unrelated values. Missing values in also columns stay missing. In key, also and key_cols columns, haven user-defined missing values (na_values, na_range) become plain missing values and the codes are dropped, because a code can't be told apart from a real identifier.

Random numbers come from R's random number generator. If your script calls set.seed() before this step, anyone with the script and the data can reproduce the assignment.

Pseudonymized data remains personal data for anyone who holds the mapping or can re-identify subjects by other means; measure the remaining risk with anon_risk().

See also

anon_subject_dates(), anon_secrets(), anon_risk()

Examples

data <- list(
  dm = data.frame(USUBJID = c("01-701-1015", "01-701-1023"), SUBJID = c("1015", "1023")),
  vs = data.frame(USUBJID = c("01-701-1015", "01-701-1023"), VSSTRESN = c(70, 80))
)
result <- anon_subject_ids(data)
result$data
#> $dm
#>   USUBJID SUBJID
#> 1  SUBJ-1      1
#> 2  SUBJ-2      2
#> 
#> $vs
#>   USUBJID VSSTRESN
#> 1  SUBJ-1       70
#> 2  SUBJ-2       80
#>
